text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Joint parliamentary-ministerial committee agree to discuss the economy next Saturday. Parliament is due to review the government's four-year programme over the coming months.
- Kuwait-Tunisia agree to boost trade to $50 million, Trade Minister Jassem al-Mudaf says.
- Rain showers flood streets in Kuwait.
- No plans to control satellite channels, Kuwait Information Minister Sheikh Saud Nasser al-Sabah says. Some 200 satellite channels can be received in the conservative Gulf Arab state.

- Kuwait's Court of Cassation on Monday upheld a five-year term for a bedoun woman, a stateless Arab residing in Kuwait, who delivered a baby boy fathered by her uncle. The boy was later sold to the defendant's Kuwaiti sister.
